corrected_content.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation
$x^{2}y^{″} - xy^{′} - 3y = 0, x > 0$.
corrected_content.worked_solution:
For a Cauchy-Euler equation, use the trial solution $y=x^\lambda.$ Then $y'=\lambda x^{\lambda-1}$ and $y''=\lambda(\lambda-1)x^{\lambda-2}.$ Substitution gives the characteristic equation
$$
\lambda(\lambda-1)-\lambda-3=\lambda^2-2\lambda-3=(\lambda-3)(\lambda+1)=0.
$$
The distinct roots are $3$ and $-1.$ Therefore, for $x>0,$
$$
y(x)=c_1x^3+c_2x^{-1}.
$$
